{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire [63:0] x, y, p, g;
    wire cin;
    wire [15:0] gp [0:4];
    wire [15:0] gg [0:4];
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result;
    wire arithmetic_enable, or_enable, and_enable;
    wire xor_enable, xnor_enable;

    // For arithmetic operations, complement only the subtrahend.
    assign x = a ^ {64{Oper[1]}};
    assign y = b ^ {64{Oper[0]}};
    assign cin = Oper[1] | Oper[0];
    assign p = x ^ y;
    assign g = x & y;

    genvar k, s, j;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : group_terms
            assign gp[0][k] = p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] &
                              p[4*k+1] & p[4*k];
            assign gg[0][k] = g[4*k+3] |
                              (p[4*k+3] & g[4*k+2]) |
                              (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1]) |
                              (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]);
        end
        for (s = 0; s < 4; s = s + 1) begin : prefix_stage
            for (j = 0; j < 16; j = j + 1) begin : prefix_column
                if (j >= (1 << s)) begin : combine
                    assign gp[s+1][j] = gp[s][j] & gp[s][j-(1 << s)];
                    assign gg[s+1][j] = gg[s][j] |
                                       (gp[s][j] & gg[s][j-(1 << s)]);
                end else begin : pass_through
                    assign gp[s+1][j] = gp[s][j];
                    assign gg[s+1][j] = gg[s][j];
                end
            end
        end
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : local_carries
            wire [3:0] c;
            if (k == 0) begin : first_group
                assign c[0] = cin;
            end else begin : later_group
                assign c[0] = gg[4][k-1] | (gp[4][k-1] & cin);
            end
            assign c[1] = g[4*k] | (p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign c[2] = g[4*k+1] |
                          (p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]) |
                          (p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign c[3] = g[4*k+2] |
                          (p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1]) |
                          (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]) |
                          (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k +: 4] = p[4*k +: 4] ^ c;
        end
    endgenerate

    assign arithmetic_enable = ~Oper[2] & ~(Oper[1] & Oper[0]);
    assign or_enable   = (Oper == 3'b011);
    assign and_enable  = (Oper == 3'b100);
    assign xor_enable  = (Oper == 3'b101);
    assign xnor_enable = (Oper == 3'b110);

    always @* begin
        sum = (arithmetic_result & {64{arithmetic_enable}}) |
              ((a | b) & {64{or_enable}}) |
              ((a & b) & {64{and_enable}}) |
              ((a ^ b) & {64{xor_enable}}) |
              ((a ~^ b) & {64{xnor_enable}});
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The three original arithmetic expressions can produce separate long carry networks followed by operation selection. Maximum arrival is expected to be dominated by carry propagation into the upper result bits.",
  "rewrite": "Share one arithmetic datapath across addition and both subtraction directions. Complement a for b-a, complement b for a-b, and inject the subtraction carry-in. Use four-bit carry-lookahead groups, a four-level parallel-prefix network across the 16 groups, and explicit local lookahead. Select arithmetic and logical results with mutually exclusive decoded masks.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The carry dependency is reduced to group formation, four prefix levels, and local lookahead instead of a long carry chain. A meaningful maximum-arrival reduction is expected, but no numerical gain is claimed without the specified mapping and STA run.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Sharing the arithmetic datapath offsets the additional prefix carry logic and introduces operand-complement control fanout. Area is expected to remain below the stated cap; mapped area and zero slew/capacitance violations still require verification with the specified flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module interface and all 64 output bits for every binary input combination. Operations 000, 001, and 010 produce a+b, a-b, and b-a modulo 2^64. Operations 011 through 110 retain OR, AND, XOR, and XNOR respectively; 111 produces zero. The original internal carry is unobservable and is omitted. No state, assumptions, undefined outputs, or external dependencies are introduced."
}
